<!--
This description is published verbatim as the release notes of a release-bound pull request (one labelled major, minor or patch). Editing the description re-runs the release-notes check where it is installed.

Release notes are generated from this description. Keep bullets short and specific, remove empty sections,
and never include prompt transcripts.

- Optional, first: a short `## Summary` of prose, or one lead paragraph (1-3 sentences, no heading), not both, and only when a theme spans the bullets.
- Sections are level 2, only these, in this order: `## Added`, `## Changed`, `## Fixed`, `## Removed`, `## Security`, `## Deprecated`. A section holding prose or `None.` is deleted, not kept.
- `(#123)` at the end of a bullet closes the issue it delivers.
- `(part of #123)` or `see #123` keeps an issue open; `Cratis/Repo#123` names another repository. One `(#123)` per issue, never `(#123, #124)`, which closes nothing: write `(#123) (#124)`. Put `(#123)` nowhere else, headings and the summary included.
- Never write `Closes #123`, `Fixes #123` or `Refs #123`, with a number or an issue URL.
- No Overview, Test plan, Verification, review notes, test or CI results, or which agent/model wrote it - those go in a pull request comment.
- Absolute https:// links only; relative links 404 on the release page.
- Replace the placeholder bullets and delete empty sections.
-->

- Short statement of what was added
